conclusion.root_cause: CashInService never calls GameAssets.burst during cash-ins, so the check sees 0 calls. The code path is correct in isolation: milestones 1/10/50/100 bypass the throttle and call GameAssets.burst(burstInfo.part.Position, tierColor, 30). The burst is only reached when GameAssets was captured and a collector was found. I could not run the 101-call scenario to confirm which of these two failed. The likeliest cause is the optional GameAssets lookup, which runs once at module load with a non-waiting FindFirstChild inside a pcall. If GameAssets is not yet parented or fails to require at that moment, the upvalue stays nil. Every burst then silently goes through the fallback `burstInfo.emitter:Emit(...)`, and GameAssets.burst is never invoked. A late or failed collector registration would produce the same result.
conclusion.evidence: GameAssets.burst exists as a function when required from the server (probe 2). Six Collector parts exist in Workspace.Plots (probe 7). The source (probe 6) shows the burst is guarded by `GameAssets and type(GameAssets.burst)=='function'` and by `burstInfo` being non-nil. If either guard fails, it uses the emitter fallback, which would produce 0 GameAssets.burst calls. This remains an unproven inference, since no probe ran the 101-call scenario.
conclusion.fix_hint: Resolve GameAssets lazily and robustly: use ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild('GameAssets', 10) or retry the require at call time when the cached value is nil, instead of a one-shot FindFirstChild at load. Make sure milestone bursts always call GameAssets.burst(pos, color, 30) before any emitter fallback, and that a collector is resolved (scanForCollectors) before the burst is skipped.
